boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Lovejoy's Station record (August 20, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. Kilpatrick's raid ran August 18-22; the Jonesborough depot (August 19) and the return march are context, and his loss figure spans the whole raid. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name Kilpatrick's and Jackson's cavalry divisions without counts; the live field reads zero. Kilpatrick says he set out with his own division, two brigades of the Second Division and two batteries, 4,500 men; that Ross's brigade was 1,100 strong and Jackson's division 4,000; and that at Lovejoy's he met a brigade of infantry. NPS names Cleburne's division as the infantry. Cox says Hood sent Jackson to meet the raid.
claims.rationale: One-side and estimated figures; the infantry's scope differs (brigade against division). None is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Kilpatrick says he was repulsed at the station, then routed Jackson's division in 'the most perfect rout any cavalry has sustained during the war', and destroyed four miles of the Macon road. Cox says no permanent interruption of the railway was made; NPS says the raiders fled to prevent encirclement and the line was running again in two days.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Kilpatrick's rout claim conflicts with the frozen result and the NPS account.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 477 (US 237; CS 240). Kilpatrick says his whole loss on the raid would not exceed 300, of whom 200 were killed and wounded; that he captured 4 guns (3 destroyed, 1 brought off) and 3 flags; and that the enemy's killed and wounded were known to be large.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Kilpatrick's figure covers August 18-22, not the frozen date alone.

open_questions: Kilpatrick's 'report of this morning' of August 23 (not found in No. 411), Murray's, Minty's and Long's reports, Jackson's and Ross's reports, Cleburne's division records and the casualty list printed with Kilpatrick's report remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Kilpatrick's August 23 dispatch and September 13 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 2, are a third family (interested Union accounts). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
